questions.q: Phenol is treated with K₂S₂O₈ in aqueous NaOH, and the product is then heated with dilute acid. The final product is:
questions.explain: The para carbon of the phenoxide attacks the peroxide oxygen, giving a 4-hydroxyphenyl sulphate; acid hydrolysis turns –OSO₃⁻ into –OH, giving benzene-1,4-diol.

questions.q: The oxidising reagent in the Elbs oxidation of phenols is:
questions.explain: Potassium persulphate (peroxydisulphate) has the O–O bond that the phenoxide attacks; potassium sulphate has no such bond, and H₂O₂/base is the Dakin reagent for hydroxy aldehydes.

questions.q: 3,4-Dimethylphenol is subjected to Elbs persulphate oxidation followed by acid hydrolysis. The product is:
options: No reaction, since the para position is blocked
questions.explain: With the para position occupied, the new OH enters ortho to the original OH, giving a catechol.

questions.q: 3-Methylphenol (m-cresol) undergoes the Elbs oxidation. The product after hydrolysis is:
questions.explain: The OH enters para to the existing OH; renumbering the resulting 1,4-diol puts the methyl next to one OH, so the product is named 2-methylhydroquinone, not a 3-substituted one.
